answer: We prove that recursive zero-knowledge reputation commitments bound to verifiable delay primitives render identity cloning information-theoretically infeasible: each agent's historic relic of attested interactions forms a hash-chained thread whose sequential depth cannot be forged, while VRF leader sortition and a falcon-derived binding signature enforce unforgeable pseudonymous transcripts, reducing Byzantine adversarial advantage beneath the finality threshold of sequential delay functions and recursive STARK finality.
